topic: Photoelectric Effect and Dual Nature of Matter
title: Dim Violet Beats Bright Red? Explained Simply | PUC Chemistry Class 11
description:
A red heater warms you for hours without a sunburn, but a few minutes of strong sunlight can burn your skin. Why does the colour of light matter more than its brightness? In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Chemistry (NCERT Chapter 2, Structure of Atom) we follow Aarav's puzzle into the photoelectric effect and the dual nature of light and matter.

On the molecule bench, packets of light hit a potassium plate. A very bright red lamp frees no electrons at all, while a dim violet lamp frees them at once, and ultraviolet makes each one faster. A frequency dial shows the threshold frequency as a gate. We build Einstein's equation step by step (h nu = h nu0 + 1/2 mv^2), work out the kinetic energy of photoelectrons from 400 nm light, and see why light is a wave when it travels (diffraction, interference) and a particle when it hits matter. Then de Broglie's bold idea that matter has waves too, the exam trap on brightness and speed, an original NEET pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

This is Episode 18 of our PUC Chemistry series.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, NEET and JEE Main students.
